scenarios.title: Home page shows hero and all three products with correct names, descriptions and prices
steps: Open /
Read the h1 and the 'Products' h2
Read each product card in the grid
expectedResults: h1 'Everyday goods, made well' with subtitle 'Small-batch essentials for your desk and kitchen.'
h2 'Products' is present in section#products
Exactly 3 cards in order: 'Ceramic Mug' / 'Hand-glazed, 350 ml.' / $18.00; 'Canvas Tote' / 'Heavyweight organic cotton.' / $24.00; 'Dot Notebook' / 'A5, 160 pages, lay-flat.' / $12.00
Each card has one button 'Add Ceramic Mug to cart' / 'Add Canvas Tote to cart' / 'Add Dot Notebook to cart' with visible text 'Add to cart'
Header cart badge shows 0 and the link's accessible name contains the badge label
scenarios.rationale: Baseline content and price formatting for the landing page; everything else depends on it.

scenarios.title: Adding products updates the header cart badge with the total quantity
preconditions: Fresh load of / (cart is in-memory only)
steps: Open /
Click 'Add Ceramic Mug to cart' twice
Click 'Add Canvas Tote to cart' once
Click 'Add Dot Notebook to cart' once
Read the header 'Checkout' link and badge after each click
expectedResults: Badge goes 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 (sum of quantities across products, not number of distinct products)
After the Mug and Tote clicks the link's accessible name is 'Checkout 3 items in cart'
Page stays on / with no navigation or reload
testData: Mug x2, Tote x1, Notebook x1 => 4
scenarios.rationale: Core add-to-cart behaviour; the badge is the only feedback the user gets.

scenarios.title: Cart badge accessible name uses correct singular grammar for one item
steps: Open /
Click 'Add Dot Notebook to cart' once
Read the accessible name of the cart badge / 'Checkout' link
expectedResults: Badge text is 1
Accessible name reads 'Checkout 1 item in cart' (singular 'item', not '1 items in cart')
scenarios.rationale: Code builds the label as `${count} items in cart` unconditionally, so a screen reader hears '1 items'; a standard accessibility/copy convention expects singular.

scenarios.title: Products added on Home carry to Checkout via client-side navigation, in catalog order
steps: Open /
Click 'Add Dot Notebook to cart' once
Click 'Add Ceramic Mug to cart' twice
Click the header link 'Checkout 3 items in cart' (client-side)
Read the order lines and summary
expectedResults: URL becomes /checkout without a full page reload
Lines: 'Ceramic Mug × 2' $36.00 and 'Dot Notebook × 1' $12.00
Subtotal $48.00 and Total $48.00
Lines follow catalog order (mug before notebook) regardless of add order
Navigating back to / via the 'Home' link keeps the badge at 3
scenarios.rationale: Verifies cart state and price calculation across the primary user flow.

scenarios.title: 'Shop all products' header link scrolls to the product list without losing the cart
steps: Open /
Click 'Add Ceramic Mug to cart' once (badge = 1)
Click the header link 'Shop all products'
Observe URL, scroll position and badge
expectedResults: URL ends with /#products and section#products (h2 'Products') is scrolled into view
Header cart badge still shows 1 (cart is not lost by a navigation link)
Link works the same from the Home page and from /checkout or /login
scenarios.rationale: The link is a plain <a href="/#products"> that triggers a full page load and silently empties the in-memory cart; users expect a nav link not to destroy their cart.

scenarios.title: Primary 'Add to cart' buttons match the Figma Button/Primary spec
preconditions: Fresh load of / at desktop viewport
steps: Open /
Inspect the computed styles of the button 'Add Ceramic Mug to cart' (repeat for the Tote and Notebook buttons)
Compare with the Home / Desktop design
expectedResults: Background #2563EB (not purple), label colour #FFFFFF, no visible border
Border radius 8px (radius/md)
Height 44px, horizontal padding 20px, label 'Add to cart' Inter 16px / 24px weight 600
Button is not stretched: about 120px wide, left-aligned inside the card
All three buttons are identical

tokens.element: the 'Add Ceramic Mug to cart' button

scenarios.rationale: Code uses --color-primary #7c3aed and .btn border-radius 2px, which differ from Figma (#2563EB, 8px); the test must catch that drift.

scenarios.title: Headings and product grid spacing match Figma typography and layout
preconditions: Fresh load of / at desktop viewport (1440x900)
steps: Open /
Inspect computed styles of the h1, the h2 'Products' and the h3 'Ceramic Mug'
Measure the horizontal distance between product cards and the container width
expectedResults: h1: Inter 40px / 48px, weight 700, colour #0F172A
h2 'Products': Inter 24px / 32px, weight 600
h3 product name: Inter 18px / 28px, weight 600
Product grid has 3 equal columns (about 341px each) with 24px gap; content container max 1120px, centred, with 24px gutters
Page background #F8FAFC; product descriptions use muted colour #475569
scenarios.rationale: Locks typography and layout tokens observed in Figma for the home page.

scenarios.title: On a 390px mobile viewport the nav collapses behind a menu button that opens and closes correctly
preconditions: Fresh load of / at mobile viewport (390x844)
steps: Open /
Check the header: logo 'Demo Shop', the 'Open menu' button and the main nav
Click 'Open menu'
Check nav links and the button's aria-expanded / accessible name
Click the menu button again
expectedResults: Header shows 'Demo Shop' and a 40x40 menu button at the right (24px gutter); nav links are hidden and nothing overflows the 390px width (matches Figma Home / Mobile)
After clicking, nav 'Main' opens as a vertical dropdown under the 64px header listing 'Home', 'Shop all products', 'Checkout N items in cart', 'Sign in to your account'; aria-expanded is true
Button's accessible name changes to 'Close menu' while open (not 'Open menu')
Second click closes the menu and aria-expanded returns to false
scenarios.rationale: Code only collapses the nav at <=320px, so at 390px the full nav is shown and the design's menu button is missing; also the toggle's aria-label never changes when opened.

scenarios.title: Mobile layout stacks hero and product cards in one column without horizontal scroll
preconditions: Fresh load of / at mobile viewport (390x844)
steps: Open /
Compare document scrollWidth with the viewport width
Read the position and size of the three product cards and their buttons
Tap 'Add Canvas Tote to cart'
expectedResults: No horizontal scrollbar; scrollWidth <= 390
h1 wraps to 2 lines (about 96px high) and content has 24px side gutters (content about 342px wide)
3 cards stacked in 1 column, each about 342px wide with 24px vertical gap, in order Mug, Tote, Notebook
Each 'Add ... to cart' button is at least 44px high, fully visible and tappable
Tapping the button increments the header badge to 1
scenarios.rationale: Home / Mobile frame defines the single-column layout; overflow from the header nav is a likely regression at 390px.

scenarios.title: Tablet viewport (834px) shows a usable header and product grid without overflow
preconditions: Fresh load of / at tablet viewport (834x1112, touch)
steps: Open /
Check the header nav items and the product grid
Tap 'Add Ceramic Mug to cart'
expectedResults: No horizontal scrolling; header logo and nav links ('Home', 'Shop all products', 'Checkout', 'Sign in to your account') are all visible on one row without overlapping or clipping
Product cards are fully readable (no truncated text) and every button is at least 44px high
Tapping the button increments the badge to 1
scenarios.rationale: No tablet design exists; general usability expectations cover the breakpoint between the 3-column desktop and 1-column mobile grids.
